name: Example release: the platform runs end to end
objective: An example charter in the shape the tooling validates (scripts/release-load.py --check). A release is one three-sprint arc: it holds the objective and decomposes it into outcomes, each a statement of what is tangibly different afterwards, written for the person the release is for, carrying a work class and the requirement criteria that prove it. Sprints hold the time box; this file holds the intent. Replace it with your own charters; keep three in planned or in_flight at all times.

outcomes.statement: A task bead carries intent and outcome only; attempt counts, leases and retries live in the workflow engine, and the conformance check fails the build when they leak into bead content.
Every edge between two beads is one of the closed link types, so a misspelt relationship is an error at write time rather than a new kind of edge.
No pull request merges without a release-gate verdict written by a fresh-context gate agent, and the merge script refuses a verdict written by the PR's own author.
The private-identifier scan runs on every pull request against the operator's own pattern file, so a host, domain or person named in a change is caught before it lands.
The retry budget for a dispatched task is owned by the workflow engine's retry policy, and nothing in bead content can raise it.
